Portfolio Architecture

Five proposed learning emphases

This portfolio overview illustrates the core management capabilities shared across our proposed executive offers. It is a curriculum design framework for evaluation, not a shared approved syllabus.

  1. Emphasis 1

    Business Foundations

    Strategic analysis, corporate finance, marketing management, operations, and managerial analytics.

    Capability BuiltTranslate functional realities into holistic financial and strategic decisions.

  2. Emphasis 2

    People Leadership

    Delegation, high-stakes feedback, executive coaching, team culture, and performance management.

    Capability BuiltMove from individual contributor excellence to inspiring and holding teams accountable.

  3. Emphasis 3

    Cross-Functional Decisions

    Stakeholder influence, inter-departmental negotiations, and enterprise resource governance.

    Capability BuiltBreak down departmental silos to align commercial, technical, and operational goals.

  4. Emphasis 4

    Workplace Application

    Action-learning project executed directly within your sponsoring enterprise or target industry.

    Capability BuiltTest management frameworks against live operational friction and enterprise realities.

  5. Emphasis 5

    Review & Reflection

    Executive panel defense, 30-day review against agreed metrics, and leadership development roadmap.

    Capability BuiltSynthesize personal leadership growth with validated organisational impact.

Stage 1: Diagnosis & FoundationsStage 5: Review & Synthesis

Format & Delivery

Learning while working

Designed for working executives and sponsoring employers to integrate rigorous capability development with demanding operational workloads:

  1. Live Discussion

    Interactive Faculty & Peer Sessions

    Faculty-moderated case analyses, simulation debriefs, and practitioner debates exploring real strategic dilemmas.

  2. Digital Support

    Self-Paced Resources & Pre-Work

    Structured readings, diagnostic toolkits, and asynchronous analytical exercises prepared before live sessions.

  3. Workplace Application

    Action-Learning Interventions

    Applied capstones addressing live operational bottlenecks, creating tangible enterprise deliverables.

Management learning, with an Indian perspective

“Our campaign proposes an Indian Knowledge Systems lens alongside practical management learning. Its role is to support discussion of leadership, judgement and responsibility in context. Specific curriculum content would require academic review.”

1. Practical Capability First

Every concept must connect to workplace execution. Tools, simulations, and frameworks are evaluated by how directly they resolve organisational friction.

2. Contextual Leadership

Examining governance, stewardship, and multi-stakeholder responsibility through indigenous philosophical traditions and Indian business ecosystem realities.

3. Purpose-Driven Execution

Leadership capability anchored in sustainable growth, societal contribution, and developing the next generation of enterprise builders across India.

Frequently asked questions

Have questions regarding this academic prototype? Reach out to the student project team through our enquiry form.

Is this an official TAPMI admissions website?

No. This website is Group 4's academic project for the Business Marketing course. It presents proposed executive and professional education offers and demonstrates a campaign-to-enquiry journey. It is not operated as an official TAPMI admissions service, and no enrolments or fee payments are processed here.

What is the difference between Sponsored and Individual EMBA?

Both pathways share the same proposed academic core and faculty standards. The Sponsored pathway adds an enterprise sponsor layer, including relationship management support, manager briefings, term-end milestone notes, and capstone alignment to a live organisational challenge (subject to learner consent).

Can professionals continue working while learning?

Yes. The proposed programmes are structured as blended part-time interventions combining live discussion, digital preparation, and workplace application so working professionals can balance ongoing operational commitments.

How does the Customised MDP cohort structure work?

The proposed Execution Leadership Accelerator is an organisational intervention for minimum 20 participants (typically 20–30 managers). It addresses an agreed business capability challenge across a 6-week blended format with four intensive workshops and a 30-day post-programme impact review.

What does the Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) lens involve?

Our campaign proposes an Indian Knowledge Systems lens alongside practical management learning. Its role is to support discussion of leadership, judgement and responsibility in context. Specific curriculum content would require institutional academic review.

How are enquiries submitted here handled?

By default, this site operates in explicit Demo Mode. Enquiries are recorded safely in your browser session for demonstration without being transmitted to external servers. Please use dummy details (e.g. @example.com) and do not submit confidential company information.

Proposed B2B Executive Pathway

Build your next generation of leaders while they keep delivering

TAPMI Executive MBA: Sponsored Leadership Pathway

A proposed employer-sponsored Executive MBA pathway for high-potential managers. The academic core is shared with self-funded learners, with a sponsor layer that connects development to a live organisational challenge.

Academic Evaluation Notice: Programme designs, fees and services shown here are student proposals for academic evaluation. They are not approved TAPMI offers or an invitation to enrol.
Target Audience

Corporate Talent Bench

HR/L&D heads, business-unit heads and corporate sponsors in technology, GCCs, services and industrial organisations looking to develop and retain high-potential talent.

Practical Value

Cross-Functional Acumen

Broader cross-functional capability; learning while working; sponsor-aligned workplace capstone; and clear sponsor communication with learner consent.

Proposed Format

Part-Time Blended

Scheduled live discussion, digital support, cases, simulations, peer learning and workplace application. Exact duration and calendar require institutional approval.

Proposed 5-Phase Learning Journey

A structured pathway that anchors foundational business knowledge directly in the sponsor's operational context:

Phase 1

Nomination & Sponsor Briefing

Candidate selection, initial sponsor alignment call, and baseline capability scoping.

Phase 2

Business Foundations

Core strategy, corporate finance, marketing management, operations, and business analytics.

Phase 3

People Leadership

Leading high-performing teams, delegation, coaching conversations, and change management.

Phase 4

Cross-Functional Decisions

Negotiation, enterprise resource allocation, stakeholder influence, and ethical governance.

Phase 5

Workplace Capstone & Review

Live organisational problem, diagnosis, intervention plan, implementation roadmap, and success measures.

Enterprise Value

The Proposed Sponsor Layer

To ensure maximum return on organizational sponsorship, the programme incorporates structured relationship management protocols:

Relationship Support

Dedicated relationship management liaison to coordinate cohort logistics, executive briefing sessions, and academic scheduling.

Term-End Progress Notes

Agreed milestone and attendance summaries shared with sponsoring HR/L&D (subject to explicit candidate consent and confidentiality agreements).

Capstone Alignment

Capstone projects are aligned directly with the sponsor's strategic initiatives, delivering measurable actionable recommendations.

Governance Note: Academic standards and grading remain the sole prerogative of the academic institution. Employment terms and bonding arrangements remain employer/employee internal matters.

Is this a different academic programme from the individual EMBA?

Can employees continue working while enrolled?

Is enrolment currently open?

No. This is an academic proposal developed by Group 4 for course evaluation. It is not an official TAPMI admissions service, and applications are not being accepted.

Proposed B2B Customised MDP

Turn a management challenge into an execution plan

TAPMI Execution Leadership Accelerator

A proposed customised Management Development Programme for middle managers and emerging business-unit leaders. The design begins with your organisation's capability gap and uses a live business problem throughout the learning journey.

Academic Evaluation Notice: Programme designs, fees and services shown here are student proposals for academic evaluation. They are not approved TAPMI offers or an invitation to enrol.
Target Audience

Middle Management

L&D and HR heads with business sponsors in GCCs, IT/services, manufacturing, BFSI, and logistics seeking structured team capability acceleration.

Proposed Format

6-Week Blended

Dedicated cohorts of 20–30 participants; 4 intensive workshops (on campus or client site); digital resources, simulations, coaching, and a 30-day impact review.

Tangible Output

Execution Action Plan

Teams formulate and defend a concrete implementation plan tackling an actual operational bottleneck with agreed success metrics.

The 6-Week Learning Journey

An 8-stage intervention structured around diagnostic scoping, execution frameworks, and post-programme accountability:

Stage 1

Diagnose

Capability diagnostic, sponsor scoping discussion, and agreeing target KPIs.

Stage 2

From Strategy to Execution

Prioritisation, cascading accountability, and decision rights.

Stage 3

Leading Through People

Delegation, high-stakes feedback, and performance coaching.

Stage 4

Cross-Functional Execution

Stakeholder alignment, cross-silo influence, and process coordination.

Stage 5

Execution Under Uncertainty

Adaptive scenario planning and data-supported managerial decisions.

Stage 6

Action-Learning Project

Teams dissect and map the sponsor's live organisational problem.

Stage 7

Executive Review

Diagnosis, proposed intervention, implementation roadmap, and KPIs presented to sponsors.

Stage 8

30-Day Impact Review

Post-programme implementation tracking against agreed business indicators.

MDP Accelerator FAQs

For whom is this accelerator intended?

It is designed for middle managers, emerging business-unit leaders, and team leads nominated by client organisations facing execution bottlenecks.

Can individual professionals enrol on an open basis?

No. The Execution Leadership Accelerator is an organisational cohort intervention requiring a minimum cohort of 20 participants sponsored by an employer.

How is the curriculum customised?

Customisation starts during Stage 1 with a diagnostic scoping call. Case examples, role-plays, and the capstone project are drawn directly from the sponsoring client's industry and internal bottlenecks.

Does this guarantee business results or ROI?

No. While the design includes agreed review metrics and a 30-day post-programme impact review, academic proposals do not guarantee external financial or business results.

Is this currently available to book?

No. This is an academic concept developed for course evaluation, not an official TAPMI admissions or corporate training offering.

Individual Pathway FAQs

Is the programme conducted entirely online?

The proposal outlines a blended delivery combining scheduled interactive live discussions, digital asynchronous study, and applied workplace exercises. Exact campus contact requirements remain unapproved.

What does the workplace capstone involve?

Participants identify a real business challenge within their current organization or industry domain, formulating a rigorous intervention with confidentiality protections and academic faculty guidance.

Who is eligible to apply?

The academic concept targets experienced mid-career professionals (typically ~5–10 years). Formal admission eligibility, degree recognition, and prerequisites would be established institutionally.

Are salary hikes or job promotions guaranteed?

No. Professional education builds capability and confidence, but career progression depends on individual performance, organizational context, and market conditions.

Can I enrol or submit an official application here?

No. This website operates strictly as an academic prototype for Group 4's coursework. No official applications or admissions transactions are processed.

About this Project

This website is a Group 4 Business Marketing student project. It presents proposed executive and professional education offers and demonstrates a campaign-to-enquiry journey. It is not operated as an official TAPMI admissions service.

Academic Project Notice: Programme designs, fees and services shown here are student proposals for academic evaluation. They are not approved TAPMI offers or an invitation to enrol.

Team Ownership & Roles

This prototype reflects distinct collaborative streams within Group 4:

Frontend & Architecture

Ayush

Owns the website implementation, faithful template adaptation, responsive design, WCAG AA accessibility, client/server validation, and Vercel serverless deployment.

CRM & Pipeline

Benjamin

Owns the CRM integration, Google Sheet database configuration, lead qualification rules, lifecycle progression, and automated candidate reminders.

Strategy & Integration

Anshita

Owns go-to-market strategy, positioning frameworks, campaign resource collateral compilation, milestone synthesis, and executive deck assembly.

Boundary Between Official Institution & Student Concept

TAPMI's official institution describes executive education and the TAPMI Centre for Executive Learning, including in-company, open, certification, and online/part-time degree offerings.

Important Clarification: Institutional context does NOT establish approval of our specific student proposals. We do not invent approval, accreditation coverage, degree recognition, eligibility, intake dates, faculty allocations, salary gains, placement rates, corporate employers, testimonials, or measured ROI. No payments, binding corporate commitments, or official applications are accepted on this prototype.

Data Governance

Privacy & Data Handling Statement

“Use dummy data for demonstrations. With your consent, an enquiry sent through the connected version may be processed by the student project team's enquiry system using Vercel, Google Apps Script, Google Sheets and the team's CRM. Do not submit confidential or sensitive information. Enquiry handling and deletion are managed by the student project team, not TAPMI admissions.”

1. Explicit Demonstration Mode

Unless verified upstream API credentials are explicitly configured by the team, the website runs in a standalone demo mode. In this mode, enquiries are logged locally in the browser session for evaluator verification. No personally identifiable information (PII) is transmitted to third-party databases.

2. Formula Injection Protection

All incoming text fields are server-side sanitized on Vercel to neutralize characters commonly used in CSV/spreadsheet formula-injection attacks (=, +, -, @, tabs, and carriage returns).

3. No Unverified Tracking or Chatbots

This website does not deploy commercial third-party behavioral tracking pixels or paid AI chatbots. Search indexing is disallowed through robots.txt and X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive HTTP headers to prevent public search engine crawling.

4. Retention & Inquiries

Enquiries submitted during demonstration will be retained solely for the duration of the academic evaluation and subsequently purged. Do not submit confidential employer data.
